chunks.title: AI Tech Stack Recommender
chunks.text:
One-liner: LLM-powered platform that recommends complete technology stacks, software architecture, deployment strategy and development roadmap from a natural language project idea.
Stack: FastAPI, React, Gemini, Python, PostgreSQL, JWT Authentication, Google Gemini, Tailwind CSS
GitHub: https://github.com/shreyad2806/AI-Tech-Stack-Recommender
Case study page: /projects/ai-tech-stack-recommender
This platform uses LLM reasoning to generate complete, practical technology recommendations in seconds, helping developers make informed decisions about their tech stack.

chunks.title: AI Tech Stack Recommender
chunks.text:
- Developers waste hours researching frameworks, databases and cloud services for every new project.
- Beginners often choose incompatible technologies or over-engineer simple systems.
- Generic tutorials don't account for project-specific requirements or constraints.
- Existing tools only answer one question instead of recommending a complete stack.

chunks.title: AI Tech Stack Recommender
chunks.text:
1. Frontend (React + Tailwind) — Modern responsive UI for project input and recommendations
2. Backend (FastAPI APIs) — High-performance Python API with typed endpoints
3. LLM Engine (Gemini) — Structured prompt engineering for consistent stack recommendations

chunks.title: AI Tech Stack Recommender
chunks.text:
- Technology Recommendation: AI suggests optimal frameworks, libraries and tools for your use case.
- Architecture Suggestions: Get a system design tailored to your project requirements.
- Backend Generation: Receive complete backend technology and API design recommendations.
- Frontend Suggestions: Get matched frontend frameworks and UI libraries.
- Database Selection: Choose the right database based on data patterns and scale.
- Deployment Strategy: Receive cloud platform and deployment pipeline recommendations.

chunks.title: AI Tech Stack Recommender
chunks.text:
- Problem: Frontend framework? Decision: React Why: Component-based architecture with a mature ecosystem for building responsive dashboards.
- Problem: Backend framework? Decision: FastAPI Why: Async Python APIs with automatic docs, type safety and excellent LLM integration.
- Problem: LLM provider? Decision: Gemini Why: Strong reasoning for structured recommendations with a cost-effective API.
- Problem: Database choice? Decision: PostgreSQL Why: Reliable relational storage for users, projects and structured recommendation data.

chunks.title: AI Tech Stack Recommender
chunks.text:
- Problem: Prompt Engineering Solution: Structured prompts with few-shot examples produced consistent JSON outputs. Learning: Clear schemas and examples dramatically improve LLM reliability.
- Problem: Recommendation Consistency Solution: Added response validation and fallback handling for malformed outputs. Learning: Always validate LLM outputs before showing them to users.
- Problem: API Latency Solution: Optimized prompts and added caching for common project types. Learning: Caching and prompt tuning matter as much as model choice.
- Problem: Structured Responses Solution: Defined strict JSON schemas that the LLM populates every time. Learning: Schemas act as guardrails for production LLM features.

chunks.title: AI Tech Stack Recommender
chunks.text:
- Natural Language Input: Yes. Describe a project idea in plain English
- Complete Stack: Full. Frontend, backend, database and deployment recommendations
- Architecture: Ready. Production-ready architecture suggestions
- Dashboard: Responsive. Works across desktop and mobile devices

chunks.title: AI Tech Stack Recommender
chunks.text:
- Prompt Engineering: Structured prompts with clear schemas are essential for reliable LLM outputs.
- LLM Integration: Integrating an LLM means balancing latency, cost, response quality and validation.
- FastAPI: Type hints and automatic docs make Python backends fast to build and maintain.
- React Architecture: Component composition and state management keep complex UIs maintainable.

chunks.title: ArchitectIQ
chunks.text:
One-liner: AI-powered software architecture review platform that analyzes repositories, identifies architectural and design issues, and produces actionable engineering insights.
Stack: Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, React, TypeScript, OpenAI, Repository Analysis, System Design, Code Intelligence
GitHub: https://github.com/shreyad2806/ArchitectIQ
Case study page: /projects/architectiq
ArchitectIQ analyzes real software repositories to identify architectural issues, design patterns, and code quality problems. It uses AI-assisted analysis to generate actionable engineering insights and recommendations.

chunks.title: ArchitectIQ
chunks.text:
- Reviewing software architecture manually is time-consuming and error-prone.
- Identifying architectural issues and design patterns requires deep expertise.
- Codebases grow complex, making it difficult to maintain architectural consistency.
- New team members struggle to understand existing architecture and design decisions.
- Automated tools often miss context-specific architectural problems.

chunks.title: ArchitectIQ
chunks.text:
1. Repository Input — Accept GitHub repository URLs or local codebases
2. Code Analysis — Parse and analyze code structure and dependencies
3. Pattern Detection — Identify design patterns and anti-patterns
4. Architecture Analysis — Analyze architectural decisions and structure
5. AI Analysis Engine — OpenAI integration for contextual analysis
6. Insight Generation — Generate actionable engineering recommendations
7. Database Storage — PostgreSQL for analysis results and history
8. API Layer — FastAPI backend for analysis services
9. React Dashboard — Frontend for viewing insights and recommendations
10. Report Generation — Generate detailed architecture reports

chunks.title: ArchitectIQ
chunks.text:
- Repository Analysis: Analyze entire codebases for architectural issues.
- Pattern Detection: Identify design patterns and anti-patterns automatically.
- Architecture Review: Review architectural decisions and structure.
- AI Insights: Generate actionable engineering insights using AI.
- Code Metrics: Calculate code quality and complexity metrics.
- Detailed Reports: Generate comprehensive architecture review reports.
- Secure Analysis: Secure handling of private repository data.
- Trend Analysis: Track architectural quality over time.

chunks.title: ArchitectIQ
chunks.text:
- Problem: Backend framework? Decision: FastAPI Why: High-performance Python APIs with async support for analysis tasks.
- Problem: AI provider? Decision: OpenAI Why: Strong reasoning capabilities for contextual architectural analysis.
- Problem: Database choice? Decision: PostgreSQL Why: Reliable storage for analysis results and repository metadata.
- Problem: Frontend framework? Decision: React Why: Component-based architecture for building analysis dashboards.

chunks.title: ArchitectIQ

- Problem: Pattern detection accuracy Solution: Combined static analysis with AI for better pattern recognition. Learning: Hybrid approaches often yield better results than single methods.
- Problem: Handling different languages Solution: Built language-agnostic analysis with language-specific parsers. Learning: Multi-language support requires modular architecture.

chunks.title: ArchitectIQ

- Analysis Engine: Complete. Full repository analysis system

chunks.title: CloseLoop
chunks.text:
One-liner: An AI-assisted financial reconciliation and exception-resolution platform that combines deterministic transaction matching with an agentic investigation workflow.
Stack: Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, XGBoost, pgvector, LangGraph, MCP.
GitHub: https://github.com/shreyad2806/razorpay-closeloop

chunks.title: CloseLoop
chunks.text: Engineers a financial reconciliation backend that combines deterministic transaction matching, ML-based exception classification, evidence retrieval and resolution recommendations. Rather than letting an LLM directly modify financial records, the system uses guardrails, provider abstraction and post-action verification.

chunks.title: CloseLoop
chunks.text:
1. Payment and settlement ingestion
2. Deterministic reconciliation
3. Exception creation
4. Evidence gathering
5. Classification (XGBoost-based exception classification)
6. Guardrail evaluation (five fail-closed guardrail gates, approval checks and idempotency controls)
7. Provider abstraction
8. Action execution (controlled resolution execution)
9. Financial state verification (post-resolution verification)

chunks.title: CloseLoop
chunks.text:
The workflow is a 17-node LangGraph graph with five fail-closed guardrail gates, approval checks, idempotency controls, controlled resolution execution and post-resolution verification (from her resume).
Tested on 30 curated financial exceptions across 9 exception types, using synthetic fixtures, SQLite unit tests and Docker-backed PostgreSQL integration tests.
There is no case-study page for CloseLoop yet; the GitHub repository is the source.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
One-liner: Enterprise compliance platform that combines RAG, local LLMs, vector search, and CrewAI-based agent orchestration for document analysis and risk detection.
Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, CrewAI, Ollama, Qwen2.5, nomic-embed-text, Pinecone, RAG, PostgreSQL
GitHub: https://github.com/shreyad2806/ComplytAI
Case study page: /projects/complytai
ComplytAI is an end-to-end compliance intelligence system that processes enterprise documents, retrieves relevant regulatory context, and uses local LLM reasoning with CrewAI orchestration to identify compliance risks and generate actionable insights.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
- Organizations manage thousands of compliance documents, policies, contracts, audit reports, and regulatory guidelines.
- Manually searching through large document collections is slow and makes it difficult to find relevant regulatory context quickly.
- Important compliance risks can be overlooked because analysts have to process large volumes of information.
- Compliance teams spend significant time reviewing repetitive documents and comparing policies against regulatory requirements.
- Traditional document search systems do not understand semantic relationships between compliance requirements, policies, and enterprise documents.
- ComplytAI combines document intelligence, RAG, local LLM reasoning, and agent orchestration to assist with compliance analysis and risk detection.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
1. Enterprise Documents — Ingest policies, contracts, audit reports, regulatory documents, and other compliance material.
2. Document Processing — Extract, clean, normalize, and prepare documents for downstream retrieval.
3. Semantic Chunking — Split documents into meaningful sections optimized for retrieval and contextual understanding.
4. Embedding Generation — Generate dense vector representations using the nomic-embed-text embedding model.
5. Pinecone Vector Database — Store document embeddings and provide scalable semantic retrieval.
6. Hybrid Retrieval — Retrieve relevant regulatory and enterprise context using semantic and keyword-based signals.
7. Ollama + Qwen2.5 — Run local LLM inference for compliance reasoning and document analysis.
8. CrewAI Agent Orchestration — Coordinate specialized agents responsible for compliance analysis, risk identification, and structured reasoning.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
9. Risk Analysis Engine — Analyze retrieved evidence and identify potential compliance risks and violations.
10. Compliance Dashboard — Present compliance findings, risk signals, evidence, and analysis results through the web application.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
- Document Ingestion: Process enterprise policies, contracts, audit reports, and regulatory documents for analysis.
- Semantic Search: Find relevant compliance information using natural-language queries instead of relying only on exact keywords.
- RAG Question Answering: Generate context-grounded answers using retrieved regulatory and enterprise document evidence.
- CrewAI Agent Orchestration: Coordinate specialized agents for compliance analysis, risk identification, and structured reasoning.
- Compliance Risk Detection: Analyze enterprise documentation to identify potential compliance risks and regulatory gaps.
- Policy Retrieval: Retrieve relevant policies, requirements, and regulatory context for specific compliance scenarios.
- Compliance Dashboard: Visualize analysis results, risk findings, and compliance insights through a centralized interface.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
- Local LLM Processing: Run Qwen2.5 locally through Ollama for privacy-conscious document analysis.
- Enterprise Knowledge Base: Maintain a searchable vector knowledge layer containing compliance documents and regulatory information.
- Evidence-Grounded Analysis: Connect compliance findings to retrieved document context rather than relying solely on model-generated information.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
- Problem: LLM choice? Decision: Qwen2.5 via Ollama Why: Provides local LLM inference for privacy-sensitive compliance workflows while reducing dependence on external model APIs.
- Problem: Embedding model? Decision: nomic-embed-text Why: Provides semantic embeddings suitable for document retrieval and enterprise knowledge search.
- Problem: Vector database? Decision: Pinecone Why: Provides scalable vector storage and efficient semantic retrieval for large document collections.
- Problem: Agent orchestration? Decision: CrewAI Why: Provides structured coordination between specialized agents while keeping individual compliance responsibilities modular.
- Problem: Backend framework? Decision: FastAPI Why: Provides high-performance Python APIs, asynchronous processing, type safety, and automatic API documentation.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
- Problem: Frontend framework? Decision: Next.js Why: Provides a scalable React-based application architecture for the compliance dashboard and user-facing workflows.
- Problem: Primary database? Decision: PostgreSQL Why: Provides reliable relational storage for application data, metadata, users, and structured compliance information.
- Problem: Retrieval approach? Decision: RAG + Hybrid Retrieval Why: Combines semantic understanding with relevant document evidence to improve retrieval quality and reduce unsupported generation.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
- Problem: Designing document ingestion Solution: Built a structured ingestion pipeline for extracting, cleaning, validating, and preparing enterprise documents for retrieval. Learning: Enterprise document processing requires robust handling of inconsistent formats, missing information, and edge cases.
- Problem: Choosing embedding models Solution: Evaluated the retrieval requirements and selected nomic-embed-text for the semantic document retrieval pipeline. Learning: Embedding quality directly affects retrieval quality, making model selection and evaluation important parts of RAG engineering.
- Problem: Handling large document collections Solution: Designed chunking and batch-processing stages to make document ingestion and indexing more manageable. Learning: Scalable AI systems require careful consideration of processing cost, memory usage, indexing strategy, and throughput.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
- Problem: Improving retrieval quality Solution: Combined semantic retrieval with keyword-based signals to improve recall across compliance queries. Learning: Hybrid retrieval can provide better coverage when queries contain both domain-specific terminology and semantic concepts.
- Problem: Reducing LLM hallucinations Solution: Used retrieved document context, structured prompts, and evidence-oriented responses to keep generated analysis grounded. Learning: Reliable LLM applications require grounding, validation, and clear boundaries around what the model is allowed to infer.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
- Problem: Coordinating compliance analysis Solution: Introduced CrewAI-based agent orchestration to separate responsibilities across compliance analysis and risk identification. Learning: Agentic systems require clearly defined responsibilities, controlled context, and reliable coordination between specialized components.
- Problem: Running AI workloads privately Solution: Integrated Ollama with Qwen2.5 to support local LLM inference for sensitive compliance workflows. Learning: Enterprise AI architecture often requires balancing model quality, privacy, infrastructure cost, and operational complexity.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text: - Problem: Building a usable compliance interface Solution: Connected the AI pipeline to a Next.js dashboard that presents analysis results and compliance findings in a structured format. Learning: AI systems become useful products only when complex model output is converted into understandable user-facing workflows.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
- AI Architecture: End-to-End. Complete document-to-analysis pipeline combining retrieval, LLM reasoning, and agent orchestration.
- RAG Pipeline: Production. Document ingestion, embeddings, vector search, retrieval, and grounded generation.
- Agentic Analysis: CrewAI. Specialized agent orchestration for structured compliance analysis.
- LLM Infrastructure: Local. Qwen2.5 inference through Ollama for privacy-conscious AI processing.
- Document Search: Semantic. Vector-based retrieval across enterprise compliance documents.
- Application: Full Stack. Next.js frontend connected to Python/FastAPI AI services and supporting infrastructure.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
- Production RAG: Production RAG requires careful attention to document processing, chunking, embeddings, retrieval quality, latency, and grounding.
- Agentic AI: Agentic systems work best when responsibilities are clearly separated and agents operate within controlled context and workflows.
- Vector Search: Retrieval quality depends on embedding models, chunking strategies, indexing, query formulation, and retrieval techniques.
- Enterprise AI Architecture: Enterprise AI systems require privacy, reliability, scalability, observability, and maintainable service boundaries.
- Local LLM Infrastructure: Running models locally introduces important engineering trade-offs around hardware, latency, model size, and privacy.

chunks.title: ComplytAI
chunks.text:
- AI Product Engineering: A useful AI product requires more than model integration; the surrounding APIs, databases, interfaces, validation, and workflows are equally important.
- Resume title: "ComplytAI – Financial Compliance and Risk Intelligence". Stack on the resume: Python, FastAPI, Next.js, CrewAI, Pinecone, RAG, Ollama, Qwen2.5.
- A five-agent CrewAI workflow for financial document analysis, anti-money laundering (AML), compliance assessment, risk auditing and executive report synthesis.
- Pinecone-based RAG using semantic retrieval, embeddings, Pydantic-validated outputs, confidence scoring and evidence citations for traceable compliance findings.
- Automated executive PDF report generation with risk scores, compliance gaps, audit flags, recommendations and supporting document evidence.

chunks.title: DevForge
chunks.text:

DevForge is a SaaS platform that enables developers to discover, build, and share reusable developer kits. It includes authentication, premium feature gating, subscription management, billing integration, and workspace functionality.

chunks.title: DevForge

chunks.title: Falcon Airlines
chunks.text:
One-liner: Full-stack airline reservation and ticketing platform with flight search, booking, payments, ticket generation, and boarding pass functionality.
Stack: Java 21, Spring Boot, Spring Security, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, JWT, React, REST APIs, PDF Generation, QR Codes
GitHub: https://github.com/shreyad2806/FalconAirlines
Case study page: /projects/falcon-airlines
Falcon Airlines is a complete airline reservation system that handles flight search, passenger booking, payment processing, ticket generation with QR codes, and boarding pass creation. Built with Java Spring Boot backend and React frontend.

chunks.title: Falcon Airlines
chunks.section_heading: What problem does Falcon Airlines solve?
chunks.text:
- Airline reservation systems require complex booking workflows, passenger management, and ticketing infrastructure.
- Traditional systems often lack modern user interfaces and seamless booking experiences.
- Generating tickets and boarding passes with QR codes requires integration of multiple technologies.
- Managing flight schedules, availability, and real-time updates is challenging.
- Payment processing and secure transaction handling are critical for airline operations.

chunks.title: Falcon Airlines
chunks.text:
1. User Interface — React-based frontend for flight search and booking
2. API Gateway — Spring Boot REST APIs handling all business logic
3. Authentication — JWT-based authentication with Spring Security
4. Flight Management — Flight schedule, availability, and pricing management
5. Booking Engine — Reservation workflow with seat selection and passenger details
6. Payment Processing — Secure payment integration and transaction handling
7. Ticket Generation — PDF ticket generation with unique booking references
8. QR Code System — QR code generation for boarding passes and check-in
9. Database — PostgreSQL for structured data storage
10. Caching Layer — Redis for session management and caching

chunks.title: Falcon Airlines
chunks.text:
- Flight Search: Search flights by origin, destination, date, and class.
- Schedule Management: Manage flight schedules, routes, and availability.
- Passenger Management: Handle passenger details, bookings, and history.
- Payment Processing: Secure payment integration for booking transactions.
- Ticket Generation: Generate PDF tickets with booking details and references.
- QR Boarding Pass: QR code-based boarding passes for check-in.
- Secure Authentication: JWT-based authentication for user accounts.
- Real-time Updates: Real-time flight status and booking updates.

chunks.title: Falcon Airlines
chunks.text:
- Problem: Backend framework? Decision: Spring Boot Why: Enterprise-grade Java framework with excellent ecosystem for building scalable REST APIs.
- Problem: Security framework? Decision: Spring Security Why: Comprehensive security framework with JWT support and authentication patterns.
- Problem: Database choice? Decision: PostgreSQL Why: Reliable relational database with strong data integrity for booking transactions.
- Problem: Caching layer? Decision: Redis Why: Fast in-memory caching for sessions and frequently accessed flight data.
- Problem: Frontend framework? Decision: React Why: Component-based architecture for building responsive booking interfaces.
- Problem: Ticket generation? Decision: PDF Libraries Why: Reliable PDF generation for tickets with custom layouts and QR codes.

chunks.title: Falcon Airlines
chunks.text: - Problem: Deployment strategy? Decision: Docker Why: Containerized deployment for consistent environments across development and production.

chunks.title: Falcon Airlines
chunks.text:
- Problem: Managing concurrent bookings Solution: Implemented database transactions and optimistic locking to handle concurrent reservations. Learning: Concurrent access requires careful transaction management and locking strategies.
- Problem: Flight availability logic Solution: Designed complex availability algorithms considering schedules, routes, and seat capacity. Learning: Business logic can become complex; break it down into manageable components.
- Problem: QR code integration Solution: Integrated QR code libraries with PDF generation for boarding passes. Learning: Multiple technology integrations require careful testing and error handling.
- Problem: Payment security Solution: Implemented secure payment flows with proper validation and error handling. Learning: Payment processing requires strict security measures and compliance.

chunks.title: Falcon Airlines
chunks.text:
- Problem: State management Solution: Used Redux for frontend state management across booking workflow. Learning: Complex workflows need predictable state management.
- Booking System: Complete. End-to-end flight booking workflow
- Ticket Generation: Functional. PDF tickets with QR codes
- Payment Processing: Secure. Integrated payment transactions
- Authentication: JWT-based. Secure user authentication
- Full Stack: Production. Complete Java + React application

chunks.title: Falcon Airlines
chunks.text:

chunks.title: Kodexa
chunks.text:
One-liner: AI developer tool for turning agent-generated and rapidly evolving codebases into reusable, maintainable software through debugging, codebase analysis, and repository intelligence.

GitHub: https://github.com/shreyad2806/Kodexa
Case study page: /projects/kodexa
Kodexa helps developers turn AI-generated code into cleaner, reusable, maintainable software. It focuses on debugging, codebase analysis, identifying duplicate/unnecessary code, improving reusability, and contextual code analysis for long-running software projects.

chunks.title: Kodexa
chunks.text:
- AI coding agents can generate duplicated, inconsistent, difficult-to-maintain code.
- Rapidly evolving codebases accumulate technical debt and redundancy.
- Identifying duplicate and unnecessary code across large projects is challenging.
- AI-generated code often lacks proper structure and reusability patterns.
- Long-running software projects need tools to maintain code quality over time.

chunks.title: Kodexa
chunks.text:
1. VS Code Extension — IDE extension for seamless developer workflow
2. Code Analysis Engine — Analyzes code structure and identifies issues
3. Duplicate Detection — Identifies duplicate and redundant code patterns
4. Reusability Analysis — Analyzes code for reusability opportunities
5. LangGraph Agents — AI agents for intelligent code analysis
6. Context Engine — Maintains context for codebase understanding
7. Vector Database — pgvector for semantic code search
8. PostgreSQL — Structured storage for analysis results
9. FastAPI Backend — API services for analysis operations
10. Refactoring Suggestions — Generates actionable refactoring recommendations

chunks.title: Kodexa
chunks.text:
- Codebase Analysis: Deep analysis of code structure and dependencies.
- Duplicate Detection: Identify duplicate and redundant code automatically.
- Reusability Analysis: Find opportunities for code reuse and extraction.
- AI Refactoring: AI-powered refactoring suggestions and improvements.
- VS Code Integration: Seamless integration with VS Code workflow.
- Code Metrics: Track code quality metrics over time.
- Contextual Analysis: Context-aware analysis considering project structure.
- Actionable Insights: Generate specific, actionable improvement suggestions.

chunks.title: Kodexa
chunks.text:

- Problem: Agent framework? Decision: LangGraph Why: Powerful framework for building agentic AI workflows.
- Problem: Vector database? Decision: pgvector Why: PostgreSQL extension for vector search, keeping everything in one database.
- Problem: Backend framework? Decision: FastAPI Why: High-performance Python APIs with async support.
- Problem: Code analysis approach? Decision: AST + AI Why: Combining static analysis with AI for better accuracy.
- Problem: Storage choice? Decision: PostgreSQL Why: Reliable database with pgvector for both structured and vector data.

chunks.title: Kodexa
chunks.text:
- Problem: Analyzing large codebases efficiently Solution: Implemented incremental analysis and caching for performance. Learning: Large codebase analysis requires optimization and caching strategies.
- Problem: Accurate duplicate detection Solution: Combined semantic similarity with structural analysis. Learning: Duplicate detection needs both semantic and structural analysis.
- Problem: Context-aware refactoring Solution: Using LangGraph agents with full codebase context. Learning: Context is critical for accurate refactoring suggestions.
- Problem: IDE integration complexity Solution: Built modular extension architecture with clear APIs. Learning: IDE extensions need careful API design and error handling.
- Problem: Balancing automation and control Solution: Provided suggestions with manual approval workflow. Learning: Developer tools should augment, not replace, developer control.

chunks.title: Kodexa

chunks.title: TalentLens
chunks.text:
One-liner: Resume intelligence platform that combines semantic search, hybrid retrieval, reranking, and structured candidate analysis to accelerate technical hiring.
Stack: Python, FastAPI, Sentence Transformers, Pinecone, RAG, Hybrid Search, Cross-Encoder, Redis
GitHub: https://github.com/shreyad2806/TalentLens
Case study page: /projects/talentlens
TalentLens is an end-to-end recruitment intelligence system that converts unstructured resumes into searchable candidate profiles. It combines document parsing, embeddings, vector search, metadata filtering, hybrid retrieval, and reranking to help recruiters identify relevant candidates faster.

chunks.title: TalentLens
chunks.text:
- Resume screening is manual and time-consuming for recruiters.
- Keyword-based ATS systems miss qualified candidates with different terminology.
- Traditional systems lack semantic understanding of candidate skills and experience.
- Recruiters struggle to find the best candidates from large resume pools.
- Existing tools don't provide explainable ranking or evidence-based candidate matching.

chunks.title: TalentLens
chunks.text:
1. Resume Ingestion — Upload and process PDF/Word resumes.
2. Document Parsing — Extract structured candidate information from unstructured documents.
3. Semantic Chunking — Split resume content into retrieval-friendly semantic sections.
4. Embedding Generation — Generate dense vector representations using Sentence Transformers.
5. Pinecone — Store and retrieve candidate vectors at scale.
6. Metadata Filtering — Filter candidates using structured attributes such as skills and experience.
7. Hybrid Retrieval — Combine semantic and keyword-based retrieval for better recall.
8. Cross-Encoder Reranking — Rerank retrieved candidates to improve relevance and precision.
9. Candidate Analysis — Generate structured candidate relevance and matching insights.
10. Recruiter Dashboard — Present ranked candidates and search results through the application interface.

chunks.title: TalentLens
chunks.text:
- Resume Parsing: Extract structured candidate information from PDF and Word resumes.
- Semantic Candidate Search: Search candidates by meaning rather than relying only on exact keyword matches.
- Hybrid Retrieval: Combine dense semantic retrieval with keyword matching to improve candidate recall.
- Cross-Encoder Reranking: Rerank retrieved candidates using a cross-encoder for higher precision.
- Metadata Filtering: Filter candidates by structured attributes such as skills, experience, and location.
- Candidate Ranking: Surface the most relevant candidates based on job-specific search criteria.
- Natural Language Search: Describe the ideal candidate in natural language and retrieve matching profiles.
- Retrieval Caching: Cache repeated operations to reduce latency and unnecessary computation.

chunks.title: TalentLens
chunks.text:
- Problem: Which embedding model? Decision: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 Why: Fast inference, low memory footprint, and good performance for resume text without the cost of larger models.
- Problem: Vector database choice? Decision: Pinecone Why: Managed service with excellent scalability, built-in hybrid search, and production-ready infrastructure.
- Problem: Backend framework? Decision: FastAPI Why: Async support, automatic API documentation, type hints, and excellent performance for I/O-bound operations.
- Problem: Chunking strategy? Decision: Semantic chunking Why: Preserves context better than fixed-size chunks, leading to more meaningful embeddings and retrieval.
- Problem: Retrieval approach? Decision: Hybrid search Why: Combines semantic understanding with keyword matching for improved recall across different query types.

chunks.title: TalentLens
chunks.text:
- Problem: Reranking method? Decision: Cross Encoder Why: Significantly improves precision by re-scoring retrieved documents with a more accurate model.
- Problem: Resume Parsing Inconsistencies Solution: Built a robust parser with multiple fallback strategies and manual validation for edge cases. Learning: Real-world data is messy; always design for exceptions and have validation pipelines.
- Problem: Embedding Quality Issues Solution: Experimented with multiple models and fine-tuned chunking parameters for optimal representation. Learning: Embedding quality depends on both model choice and how you prepare the input text.
- Problem: LLM Hallucinations Solution: Implemented strict prompt engineering with few-shot examples and output validation. Learning: LLMs need guardrails; always validate outputs and provide clear context in prompts.

chunks.title: TalentLens
chunks.text:
- Problem: Slow Retrieval Times Solution: Implemented Redis caching, optimized Pinecone queries, and added async processing. Learning: Performance optimization is critical for user experience; cache aggressively.
- Problem: Prompt Engineering Complexity Solution: Created a systematic approach to prompt design with A/B testing and iteration. Learning: Prompt engineering is an iterative process; measure and test continuously.

chunks.title: TalentLens
chunks.text:
- Resume Search: 95% faster. Compared to manual screening processes
- Hybrid Retrieval: Higher relevance. Improved candidate matching accuracy
- Architecture: Production Ready. Scalable and fault-tolerant design
- AI Stack: End-to-End. Complete RAG pipeline implementation

chunks.title: TalentLens
chunks.text:
- Production RAG: Building RAG for production requires careful consideration of latency, cost, and quality trade-offs.
- Retrieval Quality: Retrieval quality is the foundation; invest time in chunking, embedding models, and reranking.
- Evaluation: Systematic evaluation with metrics is essential; intuition alone isn't enough for AI systems.
- System Design: Design for scale from the start; caching, async processing, and error handling are non-negotiable.
